_comment: Declarative model routing for Patrick OS. Task classes name work, not vendors.
Credentials are never stored here -- only the NAME of the environment variable
that holds one. Editing this file is how you change which model does what;
no Python change should ever be required to add or retire a provider.

local-qwen._note: Same endpoint Site Factory writes against. The 24k request-body cap is the measured limit of the narrative-sourcing tunnel; it is a routing constraint, not an adapter detail.

hermes-codex._note: Reuses Hermes' existing openai-codex OAuth login; no API key is copied into Patrick OS. isolate:true adds --ignore-rules --ignore-user-config so a Patrick OS work order does not inherit Hermes' own AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, memory, or preloaded skills. extra_args is the escape hatch for flags a future Hermes version adds back (--reasoning and --safe-mode are NOT accepted by the installed v0.13.0).

openai-api._note: api_key_env is deliberately NOT plain OPENAI_API_KEY: that variable is set to the literal 'local' for the Qwen server in Site Factory's .env, and reusing it would silently send a junk key to api.openai.com.

routes._why: Mining public forums is high-volume and low-stakes. Keep it free.
Anything a human will put their name on gets the strongest writer.
Short public replies: quality matters, volume is low, cost is not the constraint.
Site Factory's hardest-won lesson (SF-07): a judge that shares a model or an answer key with the writer measures nothing. The judge must be a different provider from the writer, by construction.
Client material and candidate PII never leave the machine.
